title: Improve Observability ( LLMEvents and other System Events) in AutoGen Studio
body:
Currently, AGS shows messages exchanged by Agents (these are only the messages explicitly yielded in the agent/team implementation).
In many cases there are LLMCallEvents that are not necessarily yielded by the agents/teams (e.g., speaker selection), or even the yielded events are a subset of the actual LLMCallEvents. 

As a developer tool, it is important that AGS can let users make sense of underlying system behaviour. This can also double as data collection infrastructure.

This PR is to track efforts to show all events that occur as a team is run.

## Implementation  
- [x] Enable streaming of events to front end during run, enable storage to DB
- [x] Show a filterable log of all Events in AGS UI.

linked_prs.title: Enable LLM Call Observability in AGS
linked_prs.body: It is often helpful to inspect the raw request and response to/from an LLM as agents act. This PR, does the following: - Updates TeamManager to yield LLMCallEvents from core library - Run in an async background task to listen for LLMCallEvent JIT style when a team is run - Add events to an async queue and - yield those events in addition to whatever actual agentchat team.run_stream yields. - Update the AGS UI to show those LLMCallEvents in the messages section as a team runs - Add settings panel to show/hide llm call events in messages. - Minor updates to default team ## Why are these changes needed? ## Related issue number Closes #5440 ## Checks - [ ] I've included any doc changes needed for https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/. See https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/docs/Contribute#documentation to build and test documentation locally. - [ ] I've added tests (if relevant) corresponding to the changes introduced in this PR. - [ ] I've made sure all auto checks have passed.

ai_judgment.response: Yes. This issue involves improving the observability of LLM-related events and system behaviors in an agent system, specifically focusing on LLMCallEvents and their integration into the agent's workflow and memory storage, which aligns with the definition of an agent issue.
